key_insight: Indoor photovoltaics paired with (anti)ferroelectric energy storage and low-power computing could enable autonomous edge AI nodes that reduce reliance on centralized data centres.
engineering_relevance: Reliable distributed intelligence requires co-designing local light harvesting, energy storage and computing to match node-level power demands.
method: Assess indoor photovoltaic requirements for distributed intelligence.
Discuss emerging photovoltaic materials and remaining performance gaps.
Examine (anti)ferroelectrics for electrostatic storage and in-memory neuromorphic computing.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a perspective synthesizing opportunities and requirements, without reporting quantitative results or an integrated system demonstration.
watch_item: Reliable operation remains contingent on matching locally harvested energy to storage and computational requirements.
paper_title: Computing at the Edge Enabled by Indoor Photovoltaics and Ferroelectrics
